messages:
Maya Singh: Quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC: proposing a tiny signed 'assertion + epoch' that edge proxies carry so they can answer local reads and short-write windows without a control-plane RTT. Short sketch below.
Noah Lee: What's the threat model? We must avoid two proxies both thinking they can write.
Maya Singh: Control plane remains arbiter. It issues signed assertions with epoch numbers and caps. Only one active assertion per shard/tenant.
Asha (runtime): Token should be compact (CBOR-like) and KMS-signed. Fields: lease_id, tenant, shard_range, epoch, exp, caps. Verify fast on edge.
Kara (SRE): Need revocation path: streaming revocation vector + small bloom for immediate checks. Also tracing tags: region.intent, lease.id, lease.epoch.
Noah Lee: Sessions? WebSocket clients pinned to old lease may need migration. Options: grace window for reads or explicit transfer token signed by control plane.
Legal-Leah: Compliance: every routed request must log lease_id + region and flag cross-border writes for approval. Retention and exportability required.
Maya Singh: Canary plan: read-preference only on a subset of tenants, then a tightly supervised write canary on sandbox tenants. Metrics: p99 latency, revocation-lag, cross-region write rate, audit-log completeness.
ci-bot: Canary scheduled: eu-north read-pref 1% on 2026-06-10T03:00:00Z. Owners @Maya Singh, @Kara (SRE).
Maya Singh: Action items: Asha prototype token format; Kara prototype revocation vector and tracing; Noah pick sandbox tenants for write test; Leah draft approval checklist. Will update the RFC with diagrams.
